definitions: A type of layer in a convolutional neural network that performs an upsampling operation, effectively reversing the downsampling of a standard convolution layer. It is often used in generative models to increase the spatial dimensions of feature maps.
examples: Transposed convolution layers are crucial for image generation tasks.
The architecture utilized transposed convolution layers for upsampling.
Understanding transposed convolution layers is key to building effective decoders.
